fix(acts): a lane's restart reads the pane through the claude-input edge Acts types through, and the lane edge carries none (clno) (#827)

* fix(acts): a lane's restart reads the pane through the claude-input edge Acts types through, and the lane edge carries none (clno)

* docs(acts): the input edge's comments say who reads and who types through it (clno)

* refactor(acts): a slash line is typed only in its pane's turn (clno)
fix(test): the quiet-text sweep draws through the rig, and each row asserts the theme it drew under (s33)
fix(config): the theme resolution reads the session's pick under THEME_SETTING, the key the settings menu writes (s33)
fix(test): the quiet-text sweep draws each row under the theme it names (s33)

fix(state): each per-session file keeps its sessions' recency as list position, so an integer-like id is never moved to the oldest end (3xhn)

The session book, the session picks and the settings history each bound
their sessions by recency, and each carried that order through a record
keyed by session id: the file, and the stored state handed to a renderer.
A record enumerates integer-like keys first, so after a restart a session
like "7" written last sat at the oldest end and the bound evicted it.

Sessions now cross every hop as [id, value] entries, oldest first, and
both files are written as a JSON array of those pairs. A load takes each
pair through the session id checkpoint, refusing a repeated id by name.
A file in the keyed form is refused whole with a warning, since its order
is gone by the time it parses.

fix(daemon): a daemon's exit leaves the socket lease, so a displaced daemon can no longer unlink a newer daemon's lease (m5bq)

Removing the lease at exit was a read and then an unlink of a shared name.
A newer daemon's publish landing between the two was the lease the unlink
took, and an absent lease drains that newer daemon at its next ownership
check and lets the next EADDRINUSE reclaim its live socket. POSIX has no
unlink-if-still-mine, so no removal of the shared name can be confined to
the lease this daemon published.

Publishing is now the lease's one mutation. A lease its owner left names a
dead process identity, which arbitration reclaims as it does an absent
one, and the next publish replaces it. The unused lease path accessor goes
with the removal.
fix(daemon): a connection is one state, reads one frame, and answers an unencodable reply (df7i)
